page: Microsoft Azure E16ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at frequencies up to 4.2 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores via multithreading. The processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets, including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8 for accelerated vector and matrix computing.

The virtual machine provides 128.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included in the configuration. The instance also features no local disk storage, meaning persistent storage requirements depend entirely on remote Azure Premium Storage. Networking features zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations position the E16ns_v6 in the average category for standard multi-core compute and data manipulation. The platform achieved a PassMark CPU score of 24147.39 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 13997.69. Sustained uncached memory bandwidth registers at 116.03 GB/sec for reads and 64.51 GB/sec for writes. Database operations in PassMark reached 8573.8, while Redis SET throughput recorded 19.89 million operations per second. In machine learning inference tests, text generation for a small 135M model reached 350.76 tokens per second, placing in the top decile.

The hardware configuration trades local disk access for expanded memory capacity and specialized matrix compute extensions. This makes the instance suitable for memory-dense services relying on external block storage, including in-memory key-value databases, caching systems, analytics processing, and enterprise application backends.
